title: Commercial quantity vs small quantity - why it changes everything
p1:
A small difference in quantity can completely change the direction of a case.

Many people think the amount involved only affects the punishment. The reality is much bigger than that.
p2:
One of the most misunderstood points in drug-related offences is the difference between a small quantity and a commercial quantity.

The same substance can lead to very different legal consequences depending on where the quantity falls. A person with a smaller amount may face a different legal approach, while a commercial quantity can bring much stricter provisions, including tougher bail rules and penalties.
p3:
The surprising part? The substance alone does not decide everything. The quantity threshold set by law can completely change how authorities, courts, and defence strategies approach the matter.

Knowing this distinction helps people avoid a common mistake: assuming every possession case is treated the same.

Always look at the quantity involved before judging the seriousness of a case.
conclusion: Did you know that the quantity involved can sometimes matter as much as the substance itself? What are your thoughts on this legal distinction?
